subject: do we need to do scantwo analysis before stepwise analysis in rqtl?

messages.author: 8722bc95909a8aab
messages.subject: do we need to do scantwo analysis before stepwise analysis in rqtl?
parts:
Hello,
   Sorry, I know this is a very basic question.  I was reading the manual/instructions for stepwise regression and it seems to me that since the arguments "qtl" and "formula" are optional, then we don't really need the preliminary results from scantwo?  Is that so or am I missing something?  If that is the case, then if both, scantwo and stepwise are performed, is this for comparison purposes?

Hoping for any input,
Margarita

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] do we need to do scantwo analysis before stepwise analysis in rqtl?
parts:
On 10/03/2018 11:05 AM, Margarita Mauro wrote:
Hello,
   Sorry, I know this is a very basic question.  I was reading the manual/instructions for stepwise regression and it seems to me that since the arguments "qtl" and "formula" are optional, then we don't really need the preliminary results from scantwo?  Is that so or am I missing something?
No, you don't need the results from scantwo, or scanone for that matter.
If that is the case, then if both, scantwo and stepwise are performed, is this for comparison purposes?

scantwo results might be used to study more directly whether there are locus pairs with evidence for an interaction, or if there are chromosomes with evidence for more than one QTL.

karl

parts:

So, is there an advantage to entering information for "qtl" and "formula", from the results of scantwo/scanone?  Or better allow the program (stepwise) decide the model (qtl, formula) as it works along?

A different question, so if I see a single QTL identified in scanone and none in scantwo, then the qtl identified from scanone is still valid?  It is just not interacting with another loci, correct?
Thanks again,
Margarita

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] do we need to do scantwo analysis before stepwise analysis in rqtl?
parts: So, is there an advantage to entering information for "qtl" and "formula", from the results of scantwo/scanone?  Or better allow the program (stepwise) decide the model (qtl, formula) as it works along?

The stepwiseqtl() analysis only visits a tiny proportion of possible models. Which models get seen could be different if you try a different starting point. But the first thing that stepwiseqtl() does is perform a genome scan, so if you plug in the result from scanone() as the starting point, you'll slightly decrease computation time but won't change the results.
A different question, so if I see a single QTL identified in scanone and none in scantwo, then the qtl identified from scanone is still valid?  It is just not interacting with another loci, correct?

I wouldn't use the term "valid", but yeah if there's exactly one QTL, it may show up in scanone(), but scantwo() would not indicate any pairs of loci.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] do we need to do scantwo analysis before stepwise analysis in rqtl?
parts:
The default penalties are only for backcross and intercross and are specific to the mouse genome.
I'd suggest, as a starting point, that you use the penalties you got for the first trait.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] do we need to do scantwo analysis before stepwise analysis in rqtl?
parts:
>
> I will run permutations for several more traits and will figure out how to get the histograms. Do you mean, the histograms for each trait, for the 1000 permutations, correct?
For each trait, look at histograms for the each of the six LOD scores that are calculated in the scantwo permutations.

> If the main LOD penalty remains around 3 for several more traits, does that mean that at least I can trust my results for main effect QTLs? Or the values of the interaction LODs will somehow affect what I get for my main qtls?
>

If you use additive.only=TRUE in stepwiseqtl(), so that you're looking only for additive QTL, then only the main effect penalty will be used. But if you're looking for interactions, then everything is intertwined.

karl
